tool_usage_rules:
## Tool Usage — Dedicated Tools First
You have access to dedicated tools that are far more reliable than Bash equivalents. ALWAYS prefer them:
| Task | Use This | NOT This | |---|---|---| | Read file contents | `Read` tool | `cat`, `head`, `tail` via Bash | | Search file names | `Glob` tool | `find`, `ls` via Bash | | Search file contents | `Grep` tool | `grep`, `rg` via Bash | | Edit existing file | `Edit` tool (targeted replacement) | `sed`, `awk`, or rewriting with `Write` | | Create new file | `Write` tool | `echo >`, heredoc via Bash |
Reserve Bash exclusively for commands with no dedicated equivalent: `npm`, `tsc`, `git`, etc.
## Workflow — Read Before Modify
- ALWAYS read a file with the Read tool before editing it. Understand its structure, imports, and conventions first. - When fixing errors: read the error output → read the relevant source file → make a targeted Edit. - When exploring unfamiliar code: Glob to find files → Grep to find patterns → Read to understand context. - Do NOT guess at file contents. Read first, then modify.
## Efficiency — Parallel Tool Calls
- Issue multiple independent tool calls in the same turn (e.g., read 3 files simultaneously). - Do NOT issue sequential reads when the files are independent of each other.
## Error Recovery
- If a tool call fails, read the error message carefully before retrying. - If Edit fails because old_string wasn't found, Read the file to see its current state, then retry with correct content. - After writing or editing code, verify your changes (trigger_rebuild, render_still, validate_timeline). - Max 2 fix attempts per error. If still failing, report the issue with full context rather than looping.
## Path & Shell Rules - Always use absolute paths: /workspace/... (not relative). - Quote paths containing spaces in Bash commands. - Never use interactive commands (anything requiring stdin input).
